questions.q: Three services each contain a pasted copy of the payment code. A double-charge bug is fixed in one of them. What does moving the code into @mycompany/zudo-payments change?
questions.explain: A package turns "remember every copy" into "release once, bump three version numbers". It also forces you to decide what is public, which pasted code never does.
options: Nothing: each service still needs its own fix
The fix is made once, released as a new version, and each service picks it up by upgrading
The services no longer need tests
The bug can no longer happen, because packages are type-checked

questions.q: Why is @zudojs/errors a peerDependency of the payments package rather than a regular dependency?
questions.explain: With a regular dependency, npm may install a private copy for your package whenever the versions differ. Two copies mean two class hierarchies, which breaks instanceof and any module-level state.
options: Peer dependencies install faster
Regular dependencies cannot be imported at run time
So the app's own copy is used: one BaseError class in the process, and instanceof and error handling keep working
npm refuses to publish packages that depend on scoped packages

questions.q: The same @zudojs packages are listed in both peerDependencies and devDependencies. Why both?
questions.explain: Installing your package in an app never installs its devDependencies. In your repository, though, you need a real copy to compile and test against, and devDependencies provide it.
options: It is a mistake; one of them is ignored
Peer says "the app must provide it"; dev installs it in your own repository so you can build and run the tests
devDependencies are published, peerDependencies are not
It makes npm install two copies on purpose

questions.q: Why does createFakeProvider live in its own entry point, @mycompany/zudo-payments/testing?
questions.explain: A separate entry makes the purpose visible in every import line. It is still published: apps need it for their tests.
options: Because Node can only load one function per entry point
So production code does not import a test helper by accident, while apps can still use it in their own tests
Because test code must be CommonJS
So it is left out of the tarball

questions.q: With "files": ["dist"], which of these ends up in the tarball?
questions.explain: files is an allow-list, and npm adds the manifest, README and license on its own. npm pack --dry-run shows the real list; the lesson's check found no sources, tests or configuration.
options: Only the dist folder
dist, plus package.json, the README and the LICENSE, which npm always includes
dist and src, because the declarations refer to it
Everything not listed in .gitignore

questions.q: The package's src/index.ts uses export { A, B } from "./x.js" and never export * from. What does that protect against?
questions.explain: export * publishes whatever the file exports, today and in the future. Named re-exports make each public name a decision, like the barrels of @zudojs/adapters and @zudojs/plugins.
options: Slower builds
Circular imports
A helper added to a file later becoming public API by accident
Declaration files being skipped

questions.q: dist/internal/money.js is inside the published tarball. Can an app import it?
questions.explain: The file must ship because the service needs it at run time. Being in the tarball is not the same as being importable; the exports map decides that.
options: Yes, with @mycompany/zudo-payments/internal/money
Yes, with @mycompany/zudo-payments/dist/internal/money.js
No: no entry of the exports map leads to it, so Node refuses both paths with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
No, because npm removes files named "internal"

questions.q: Why are all amounts in the package integers in kobo instead of naira with decimals?
questions.explain: Binary floating point cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly. Integers up to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER are exact, which is why the service rejects anything that is not a safe positive integer.
options: JavaScript numbers cannot hold decimals
Integer arithmetic on money is exact, while decimals like 0.1 + 0.2 are not, and the provider's API uses kobo too
Kobo values are smaller, so they use less memory
TypeScript cannot type decimal numbers

questions.q: A card is declined. Which base class and status fit PaymentDeclinedError best?
questions.explain: The provider worked correctly; it said no. That is a business outcome, exposed to the customer so they can try another card. 502 would claim your provider failed, and 500 would hide the reason.
options: ExternalServiceError, 502
DomainError with status 402: a normal business outcome the customer must see
ValidationError, 400
Plain Error, 500

questions.q: Why does PaymentProviderError reach the client as "An unexpected error occurred." instead of its own message?
questions.explain: A provider name, "ECONNRESET" or a hostname helps an attacker and means nothing to a customer. expose: false keeps them internal, and cause keeps the original for your log.
options: Because its constructor forgets to pass the message
Because ExternalServiceError is not exposed by default, so the public serializer replaces the message; the details stay on the error for the logs
Because status 502 errors cannot have messages
Because the cause is an Error

questions.q: Why does isPaymentError check isBaseError(value) && value.code.startsWith("ERR_PAYMENT_") instead of value instanceof PaymentDeclinedError || …?
questions.explain: isBaseError falls back to a brand from the global symbol registry, and codes are plain strings, so both survive duplicate copies. The prefix also means a new error class is covered without changing the function.
options: Because instanceof does not work with classes
It keeps working if the app ends up with two copies of the package or of @zudojs/errors, and it covers every current and future payment error in one rule
Because codes are faster to compare than prototypes
Because the error classes are not exported

questions.q: You want to rename ERR_PAYMENT_DECLINED to ERR_CARD_DECLINED. No function signature changes. Which version bump is it?
questions.explain: Error codes are part of the public API precisely because clients branch on them. Add a new code if you must, keep the old one, and remove it only in a major.
options: Patch: only a string changes
Minor: it is an improvement
Major: clients compare the code, and theirs would silently stop matching
None: codes are internal

questions.q: A customer double-clicks "Pay". Both requests reach payments.charge with reference ORD-1001 while the provider is still answering the first. What happens?
questions.explain: The service keeps the promise of every charge in progress, keyed by reference, and a completed payment in a second map. Only a different amount under the same reference is a conflict.
options: The provider is called twice and the card is charged twice
The second request fails with ERR_PAYMENT_CONFLICT
The second request finds the first one's promise in the in-flight map and gets the same payment; the provider is called once
The second request waits one second and tries again

questions.q: Order ORD-1001 was charged ₦12,500. Later a request arrives with the same reference and ₦9.99. What should the service do, and why?
questions.explain: An idempotency key promises "this is the same operation". Different content under the same key means that promise is broken, so fail loudly with ERR_PAYMENT_CONFLICT.
options: Charge ₦9.99, because it is a new request
Return the ₦12,500 payment silently
Throw a 409 conflict: the same idempotency key with a different body is a bug in the caller, and guessing either way could be wrong
Refund the first charge and charge again

questions.q: Why does createPaystackProvider accept a fetch option?
questions.explain: Injecting the one function that touches the network makes the adapter fully testable: the tests check the URL, headers and body that would have been sent.
options: Because Node 24 has no global fetch
So tests can pass a fake that records requests and returns canned responses, with no network and no real charges
To make the adapter faster
Because Paystack requires a custom fetch

questions.q: The adapter's 15-second timeout fires during a charge. What do you know about the customer's card?
questions.explain: A timeout is the third outcome of a network call: unknown. Reporting "failed" can lead to a second charge; the fix is to ask the provider about that reference, or wait for its webhook.
options: It was not charged
It was charged
Nothing: the charge may have happened with the answer lost, so you must find out (by reference) before telling the customer or retrying
It was charged twice

questions.q: You add a required method verify(reference) to the exported PaymentProvider interface. Your own service calls it. Which bump is honest?
questions.explain: Adding to an interface people call is safe; adding a required member to an interface people implement breaks them. Add it as optional in a minor, then make it required in the next major.
options: Patch, because callers of createPaymentService change nothing
Minor, because a method was added
Major, because anyone who implemented PaymentProvider for their own provider no longer compiles
No bump: interfaces are erased at run time

questions.q: An app depends on "@mycompany/zudo-payments": "^0.1.0". You publish 0.2.0. Does the app get it on its next fresh install?
questions.explain: ^0.1.0 means >=0.1.0 <0.2.0. That is why, in 0.x, a breaking change bumps the minor.
options: Yes, a caret accepts every newer minor
No: below 1.0.0 a caret only accepts patches (0.1.x), because in 0.x the minor number signals breaking changes
Yes, but only with --force
No, carets never accept new versions

questions.q: When is a changeset file written in the changesets workflow?
questions.explain: The person who knows whether a change breaks anything records it when they make it. changeset version later adds all pending files up into version bumps and changelog entries.
options: By the release manager, once per release, from memory
By the author, in the same pull request as the change, naming the package, the bump and a changelog sentence
Automatically by npm when you publish
By CI, from the commit messages

questions.q: Three pending changesets for the package say: patch, minor, patch. The package is at 0.1.0 (and you treat minors as features). What does changeset version produce?
questions.explain: The highest bump wins and is applied once. All three sentences still appear in CHANGELOG.md, grouped under minor and patch changes.
options: 0.2.0, with one changelog entry per changeset

questions.q: The manifest has "prepublishOnly": "npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build". When does it run?
questions.explain: prepublishOnly is the last gate before a release. npm pack does not run it, which is why the lesson builds first and then checks the tarball.
options: On every npm install
On npm pack
Before npm publish uploads anything; if a step fails, nothing is published
Only in CI

questions.q: validateAll from @zudojs/docs reports a BROKEN_LINK warning and valid: true. Your CI script only checks valid. What happens?
questions.explain: Only errors make a result invalid; broken links are warnings. Fail the build on any issue (the lesson's script sets process.exitCode), or on the warning codes you care about.
options: The build fails
The build passes and the README ships with a link to a page that does not exist
The broken link is removed automatically
npm refuses to publish

questions.q: A script at the root of the package does import … from "@mycompany/zudo-payments" and it works, although nothing is installed under that name. Why?
questions.explain: Package self-referencing makes the script a faithful consumer: it can only reach what the exports map allows, so the internal-import test in the lesson proves what an app would see.
options: npm links every package into its own node_modules
Node lets a package import itself by its own name when its package.json has an exports map, going through the same entry points as any app
TypeScript rewrites the import to ./src/index.ts
The name is resolved from the npm registry

questions.q: You lower the default maxAmountKobo from ₦5,000,000 to ₦1,000,000. No types change. Which bump?
questions.explain: Behaviour is part of the contract, not only signatures. A stricter default breaks working callers even though every call still compiles.
options: Patch
Minor
Major: a charge of ₦2,000,000 that worked yesterday now fails for every app that relies on the default
None, because defaults are not API

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: BaseError sets name from the class actually constructed, and toString prints name, code and message. DomainError supplies the business category and expose: true; the 402 given here replaces its default 422.
options:

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: An ExternalServiceError is not exposed by default, so the public view replaces the message and leaves out the metadata, including the service name. The internal address never reaches the client.
options: {"code":"ERR_PAYMENT_PROVIDER","message":"An unexpected error occurred.","category":"external_service","statusCode":502}
{"code":"ERR_PAYMENT_PROVIDER","message":"Provider paystack failed: ECONNRESET 10.0.4.7","category":"external_service","statusCode":502}
{"code":"ERR_PAYMENT_PROVIDER","message":"An unexpected error occurred.","category":"external_service","statusCode":502,"metadata":{"service":"paystack"}}
{"message":"Internal Server Error","statusCode":500}

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A validation error defaults to 400 and is exposed, because the client can fix its input. issueCount counts every issue and issuesForField filters by field.
options: 400 3 2 true
422 3 2 true
400 2 1 true
400 3 2 false

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Zero and negatives fail > 0. 12.5 is not an integer, 2 ** 53 is beyond the safe integer range, and Number.isSafeInteger never converts strings.
options: true false false false false false
true true false false true true
true false false false true false
true false true false false true

questions.q: A reduced version of the service's idempotency. What does it print?
questions.explain: The concurrent pair shares the in-flight promise. The third call finds the completed payment, the same object. Only ORD-2 calls the provider again: two calls in total.
options: true true 2
false false 4
true false 2
true true 3

questions.explain: Turning the arguments into a real Request lets a test read the method, URL, headers and body exactly as they would have been sent. Response.json builds the canned answer. No network is involved.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A signal from AbortSignal.timeout aborts with a DOMException named TimeoutError, which a real fetch rejects with. A manual controller.abort() would give AbortError. Compare names, not messages: messages differ between runtimes.
options: TimeoutError
AbortError
answered
Error

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The highest pending bump is applied once. A minor or major bump resets the numbers to its right, and version parts are numbers, so 9 + 1 is 10, not a carry.

questions.q: This implements the caret rule for plain versions. What does it print?
questions.explain: For 1.x and above a caret allows anything with the same major. Below 1.0.0 the first non-zero number is treated as the major, so ^0.1.0 stops before 0.2.0.
options: true false true false
true false true true
true true true true
false false true false

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: ConflictError supplies 409 and expose: true. A plain Error is not a BaseError, so it fails the first half of the check even though its message contains the prefix: the check reads code, never the message.
options: 409 true true false
409 false true false
400 true true true

questions.q: Write PaymentDeclinedError: it extends DomainError from @zudojs/errors, takes a reference and a reason, uses code ERR_PAYMENT_DECLINED, status 402, and stores both values in metadata. The program should print PaymentDeclinedError ERR_PAYMENT_DECLINED 402 Insufficient Funds.
questions.explain: Pass the code, status and metadata to the base constructor; everything else (category, severity, expose, name) comes from DomainError and BaseError.

questions.q: Write validate(request): collect an issue for each problem (reference empty; email without @; amountKobo not a safe positive integer) and, if there are any, throw a ValidationError with code ERR_PAYMENT_INVALID and the issues. The program should print ERR_PAYMENT_INVALID email,amountKobo.
questions.explain: Collect every problem before throwing, so the client can fix all fields in one round trip instead of discovering them one request at a time.

questions.q: Write isPaymentError(value) with isBaseError from @zudojs/errors and the code prefix ERR_PAYMENT_. The program should print true false false.
questions.explain: The NotFoundError is a BaseError with another code, and a string is not an error at all. Checking isBaseError first also guarantees that code is a string before you call startsWith.

questions.q: Complete charge so that concurrent calls with the same reference share one provider call, a completed reference returns the stored payment, and a completed reference with a different amount throws an error whose message is conflict. The program should print calls: 1, then conflict.
questions.explain: Two maps cover the two moments: in flight (share the promise) and completed (return the stored result). The amount check makes a reused key with a different body fail instead of silently returning the wrong payment.

questions.q: Write toResult(body), the adapter's mapping: throw an Error with message refused: MESSAGE when body.status is false; otherwise return { status: "success", providerReference } for data.status === "success", or { status: "failed", providerReference, reason } using gateway_response. The program should print the three lines shown in expected.
questions.explain: The adapter's only job is translation: provider JSON in, your types out. A refused request is an error; a declined card is a normal result with a reason, which the service turns into PaymentDeclinedError.

questions.q: A public-API snapshot test compares what an entry point exports with an approved list. Write diffApi(actual, approved) returning { added, removed } (sorted arrays). The program should print added: formatKobo | removed: isPaymentError.
questions.explain: An added name (here an internal helper that leaked out) needs a decision and at least a minor bump; a removed name is a breaking change. In a real test, actual is Object.keys(await import("@mycompany/zudo-payments")).

questions.q: Write createFakeProvider({ decline }): its charge(request) records the request in requests, returns { status: "failed", reason: "Insufficient Funds" } when request.authorizationCode is in decline, and { status: "success" } otherwise. The program should print success failed 2.
questions.explain: A fake driven by its inputs lets each test choose the outcome it needs, and the recorded requests let it assert what was sent. Shipping it under /testing saves every app from writing its own.
